about: Current map generator settings (the engine values as of 2026-10-01). worldgen/worldgen.js uses these as WorldGen.DEFAULTS; WorldGen.settingsFromJson(thisFile) reads this file back. Explained in docs/02_WORLD.md.
noiseFormula: For each octave o = 0..Octaves-1: Sum += PerlinNoise2D(X * PatternScale * 2^o / NoiseScale + Seed, Y * PatternScale * 2^o / NoiseScale + Seed) / 2^o. Value = Sum * Multiplier + Offset. X, Y = tile column and row. Seed = the layer's seed (only seed mod 256 matters).

width.meaning: Map width. One tile is a 2.5 km square.

startClear.meaning: Tiles within this distance of the centre tile (counted like a king moves in chess) are always empty: no island, big island or water object. 1 = the 3x3 block around the centre tile; 0 = off.

islandPattern.meaning: Islands noise, Pattern Scale. Larger = smaller, denser shapes. Only Pattern Scale / Noise Scale matters.

islandNoise.meaning: Islands noise, Noise Scale. Larger = bigger, clumpier land shapes. If Noise Scale / Pattern Scale is 1, 2, 4, 8 ..., some octaves fall on whole coordinates and add nothing (1 = no land at all).

islandOctaves.meaning: Islands noise, octaves (layers of detail). More = more ragged coasts and specks of land.

islandOffset.meaning: Added to the islands noise value. Positive = more land.

islandMultiplier.meaning: Multiplies the islands noise sum before Offset.

islandThreshold.meaning: Perlin Modifier: the land threshold. A tile whose islands noise value is above it is land (one small island). Higher = fewer islands.

bigPercent.meaning: Big island %: each biome gets round(this x its small-island count) big islands (2x2 stamps).

biomePattern.meaning: Biomes noise, Pattern Scale. Larger = smaller biome areas.

biomeNoise.meaning: Biomes noise, Noise Scale. Larger = wider biome areas.

biomeOctaves.meaning: Biomes noise, octaves. More = more ragged biome borders.

biomeOffset.meaning: Added to every biome value: positive shifts the map towards Desert, negative towards Polar.

biomeMultiplier.meaning: Stretches biome values away from 0: above 1, the edge biomes (Polar, Desert) get more room.

subOn.meaning: Sub-biomes. Off in the game. When on, an interval that names two or three biomes is split between them by a separate noise.

subPattern.meaning: Sub-biomes noise, Pattern Scale (used only when subOn is true).

waterMode.meaning: What happens when several water objects claim one water tile. competition (the game today): the highest noise value takes it, the others lose it; a tie goes to the earlier row. parallel (planned mechanic): every claimant keeps it, so one tile can hold up to three objects.

biomeFields.min: Lowest biome-noise value of the interval (inclusive).
biomeFields.max: Highest value (exclusive). Values outside every interval go to the nearest interval, so the ends also take values below -1 or above 1.
biomeFields.names: The biome of the interval. Two or three names only matter when sub-biomes are on. An interval with min = max is switched off.

waterObjectFields.key: Short id used in WorldGen output (map.water.<key>).
waterObjectFields.name: Display name.
waterObjectFields.noiseScale: Noise Scale of the object's own noise.
waterObjectFields.patternScale: Pattern Scale of the object's own noise.
waterObjectFields.octaves: Octaves of the object's noise (4 for each: the team's answer, the engine panel does not show it).
waterObjectFields.multiplier: Multiplies the noise sum before Offset.
waterObjectFields.threshold: The object claims a water tile where its noise value is above this. Higher = fewer tiles.
waterObjectFields.on: false = the object is not generated.
